BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. ## PR Description

### What changed
The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. # gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

## PR Description

### What changed
The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.

- Release-bump carve-out (owner-authored `chore/release-v*`) unchanged and independent of the list.

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

Effect of (b): for an owner-authored release-bump PR with validation-red, the SM would now try github_get_pr + parse body for `closes #N` + branch fallback — branch is `chore/release-vX.Y.Z`, which doesn't match `/gh-(\d+)$/` → linked stays null. What does the machine path do differently vs guest path? Per the superseded 2026-10-04 comment: validation-red arms rework for guests too, PR-anchored. So the difference: machine PRs arm rework on the linked issue; guests get PR-anchored arm. For release-bump, linked is null → probably falls to the same PR-anchored arm. So effect may be minor but it's a semantic change not mentioned in the PR description ("Release-bump carve-out unchanged and independent of the list") — actually the carve-out in isMachineAuthored was pre-existing for the review guards; extending it to the rework re-arm is new behavior. Is it harmful? If a release-bump PR fails validation, now the machine tries to parse body for closing keywords — a release-bump body might contain "closes #..." rarely. Minor risk: it could arm rework on some issue referenced in the release notes. Edge case.

Also effect of (a) case-sensitivity: previously case-insensitive compare of ticket.author. If ticket.author arrives with different casing than config... GitHub API returns canonical login. Low risk.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. ## PR Description

### What changed
The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.

### Key decisions
- `resolveMachineAuthor` still returns the raw config string; new `machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties, null → `[]` fail-closed); `isMachineAuthored` matches PR authors with a **case-sensitive** exact compare per entry; new `isMachineLogin()` gives the park probes their historical case-insensitive actor match across all entries.
- Swept every direct single-login compare: the `fail_validation` rework re-arm in `smAgent.js`, both sticky-park RESET freshness checks, `parkResetCommit`'s machine-merge walk, the PR-anchored rework re-arm in `postPRReviewComments.js`, and `factoryState.js` `in_dev` assignment bucketing — all now route through the shared helpers.
- `.github/workflows/machine-sm.yml` input becomes `'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'`; module + factory docs updated.
- Release-bump carve-out (owner-authored `chore/release-v*`) unchanged and independent of the list.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
```
1566 pass; 3 failures in `release workflow wiring` are pre-existing on main (they assert on `agent-pack-release.yml`, untouched here).

flowchart TD
  CFG["machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'"] --> RAW["resolveMachineAuthor (raw string)"]
  RAW --> LIST["machineAuthorLogins() -> [ai-teammate, github-actions[bot]]"]
  LIST --> AUTH["isMachineAuthored (PR authors, case-sensitive)"]
  LIST --> LOGIN["isMachineLogin (commit actors, case-insensitive)"]
  AUTH --> GUARDS["prMachineAuthor gate · notMachine filter · rework re-arms"]
  LOGIN --> PARK["sticky-park RESET / parkResetCommit walk"]
  LIST --> BUCKET["factoryState in_dev bucketing"]
```

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

Now: `isMachineAuthored(ticket, machineAuthor, owner)` which (a) is case-sensitive, (b) includes the release-bump carve-out (owner-authored `chore/release-v*` PRs now count as machine).

Effect of (b): for an owner-authored release-bump PR with validation-red, the SM would now try github_get_pr + parse body for `closes #N` + branch fallback — branch is `chore/release-vX.Y.Z`, which doesn't match `/gh-(\d+)$/` → linked stays null. Then below, presumably machine PRs with no linked issue... let me read further to see what happens when isMachinePr and linked==null. For a release-bump PR this now routes through the machine path. What does the machine path do differently vs guest path? Per the superseded 2026-10-04 comment: validation-red arms rework for guests too, PR-anchored. So the difference: machine PRs arm rework on the linked issue; guests get PR-anchored arm. For release-bump, linked is null → probably falls to the same PR-anchored arm. So effect may be minor but it's a semantic change not mentioned in the PR description ("Release-bump carve-out unchanged and independent of the list") — actually the carve-out in isMachineAuthored was pre-existing for the review guards; extending it to the rework re-arm is new behavior. Is it harmful? If a release-bump PR fails validation, now the machine tries to parse body for closing keywords — a release-bump body might contain "closes #..." rarely. Minor risk: it could arm rework on some issue referenced in the release notes. Edge case.

Also effect of (a) case-sensitivity: previously case-insensitive compare of ticket.author. If ticket.author arrives with different casing than config... GitHub API returns canonical login. Low risk.

## PR Description

### What changed
The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.

- Release-bump carve-out (owner-authored `chore/release-v*`) unchanged and independent of the list.

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

Key observations:

1. In smAgent.js line ~2334, `isMachinePr` previously: `!!machineAuthor && !!ticket.author && String(ticket.author).toLowerCase() === String(machineAuthor).toLowerCase()` — a pure author compare, case-insensitive, NO release-bump carve-out. Now: `isMachineAuthored(ticket, machineAuthor, owner)` which (a) is case-sensitive, (b) includes the release-bump carve-out (owner-authored `chore/release-v*` PRs now count as machine).

Effect of (b): for an owner-authored release-bump PR with validation-red, the SM would now try github_get_pr + parse body for `closes #N` + branch fallback — branch is `chore/release-vX.Y.Z`, which doesn't match `/gh-(\d+)$/` → linked stays null. Then below, presumably machine PRs with no linked issue... let me read further to see what happens when isMachinePr and linked==null. For a release-bump PR this now routes through the machine path. What does the machine path do differently vs guest path? Per the superseded 2026-10-04 comment: validation-red arms rework for guests too, PR-anchored. So the difference: machine PRs arm rework on the linked issue; guests get PR-anchored arm. For release-bump, linked is null → probably falls to the same PR-anchored arm. So effect may be minor but it's a semantic change not mentioned in the PR description ("Release-bump carve-out unchanged and independent of the list") — actually the carve-out in isMachineAuthored was pre-existing for the review guards; extending it to the rework re-arm is new behavior. Is it harmful? If a release-bump PR fails validation, now the machine tries to parse body for closing keywords — a release-bump body might contain "closes #..." rarely. Minor risk: it could arm rework on some issue referenced in the release notes. Edge case.

Also effect of (a) case-sensitivity: previously case-insensitive compare of ticket.author. If ticket.author arrives with different casing than config... GitHub API returns canonical login. Low risk.

2. postPRReviewComments.js: previously `prAuthor === machineAuthor` — strict, case-sensitive single compare, no carve-out. Now isMachineAuthored adds release-bump carve-out. Same semantic expansion. For owner-authored release-bump PR with REQUEST_CHANGES review — now re-arms agent:rework on linked issue. Review on release-bump is unlikely but change in behavior.

These are worth flagging as IMPORTANT (behavioral widening beyond ticket scope — the ticket says "Update isMachineAuthored" for author guards and "sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login — they all ride isMachineAuthored". Actually ticket item 4 says: "Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly." The smAgent rework re-arm and postPRReviewComments re-arm were direct compares — the PR swept them through isMachineAuthored, which is per ticket intent (they should ride the shared predicate). But the release-bump carve-out inclusion is a side effect. Is it a bug? Consider: release-bump PRs are owner-authored; if review requests changes on them, previously: external path (verdict comment only). Now: re-arm agent:rework on the linked issue. A release bump rarely has a linked issue with "closes #N". So impact small. I'd classify SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT? The review verdict rules say IMPORTANT = real maintainability debt. It's a subtle behavior change; flag as SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT. I'll say IMPORTANT-lite → I'll classify SUGGESTION with clear explanation, or IMPORTANT. Hmm. Given "when in doubt, start one level higher" — but also anti-pattern of blocking on nits. This isn't blocking. I'll mark IMPORTANT for the semantic widening, since it changes behavior for owner-authored release-bump PRs in a way not covered by tests.

Actually wait — is it a *correct* change arguably? If a release-bump PR fails validation, treating it as machine-owned could be desired (release flow is automated). But the release-bump flow doesn't have a rework loop — arming agent:rework on some issue could be wrong. It's ambiguous → SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT. I'll go IMPORTANT.

3. factoryState.js: `!!(issue && issue.assignee && issue.assignee.login !== undefined && logins.indexOf(issue.assignee.login) !== -1)` — fine.

4. machine-sm.yml: input `'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'` quoted in YAML — good since comma+brackets. But wait: does the factory-sm.yml reusable workflow declare machine-author as a string input and does it do any parsing/validation? Also, does anything downstream compare the machine-author input as a single login in the dmtools-agentic-workflows repo? That's a different repo (factory workflows). Out of scope here, but worth noting? The docs say factory-sm contract accepts the string. Can't verify external repo. Note as a consideration in general comment maybe.

5. Case-sensitivity of isMachineAuthored per entry: documented as design. Previously `itemAuthor(item) === machineAuthor` was also case-sensitive. Unchanged. Good.

6. In smAgent park probes (machinePushVf, vprMachinePush): previously `actorLoginVf === machineLoginVf` where actorLoginVf lowercased and machineLoginVf lowercased; empty actor login meant machinePushVf false. New: isMachineLogin('' , ...) returns false. Same fail-closed. Good. Note in vpr probe: previously `!!vprMachineLogin && vprActorLogin === vprMachineLogin`; now isMachineLogin handles null. Good.

7. parkResetCommit: machineMerge check now `!!login && machineAuthorModule.isMachineLogin(commit.login, machineAuthor)` — passes original-case login, isMachineLogin lowercases internally. Fine.

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.

- Release-bump carve-out (owner-authored `chore/release-v*`) unchanged and independent of the list.

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

Effect of (b): for an owner-authored release-bump PR with validation-red, the SM would now try github_get_pr + parse body for `closes #N` + branch fallback — branch is `chore/release-vX.Y.Z`, which doesn't match `/gh-(\d+)$/` → linked stays null. What does the machine path do differently vs guest path? Per the superseded 2026-10-04 comment: validation-red arms rework for guests too, PR-anchored. So the difference: machine PRs arm rework on the linked issue; guests get PR-anchored arm. For release-bump, linked is null → probably falls to the same PR-anchored arm. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

## PR Description

### What changed
The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.

- Release-bump carve-out (owner-authored `chore/release-v*`) unchanged and independent of the list.

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

Now: `isMachineAuthored(ticket, machineAuthor, owner)` which (a) is case-sensitive, (b) includes the release-bump carve-out (owner-authored `chore/release-v*` PRs now count as machine).

Effect of (b): for an owner-authored release-bump PR with validation-red, the SM would now try github_get_pr + parse body for `closes #N` + branch fallback — branch is `chore/release-vX.Y.Z`, which doesn't match `/gh-(\d+)$/` → linked stays null. Then below, presumably machine PRs with no linked issue... let me read further to see what happens when isMachinePr and linked==null. For a release-bump PR this now routes through the machine path. What does the machine path do differently vs guest path? Per the superseded 2026-10-04 comment: validation-red arms rework for guests too, PR-anchored. So the difference: machine PRs arm rework on the linked issue; guests get PR-anchored arm. For release-bump, linked is null → probably falls to the same PR-anchored arm. So effect may be minor but it's a semantic change not mentioned in the PR description ("Release-bump carve-out unchanged and independent of the list") — actually the carve-out in isMachineAuthored was pre-existing for the review guards; extending it to the rework re-arm is new behavior. Is it harmful? If a release-bump PR fails validation, now the machine tries to parse body for closing keywords — a release-bump body might contain "closes #..." rarely. Minor risk: it could arm rework on some issue referenced in the release notes. Edge case.

Also effect of (a) case-sensitivity: previously case-insensitive compare of ticket.author. If ticket.author arrives with different casing than config... GitHub API returns canonical login. Low risk.

2. postPRReviewComments.js: previously `prAuthor === machineAuthor` — strict, case-sensitive single compare, no carve-out. Now isMachineAuthored adds release-bump carve-out. Same semantic expansion. Consider: release-bump PRs are owner-authored; if review requests changes on them, previously: external path (verdict comment only). Now: re-arm agent:rework on the linked issue. A release bump rarely has a linked issue with "closes #N". So impact small. I'd classify SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT? The review verdict rules say IMPORTANT = real maintainability debt. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.
