# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## PR Description

### What changed
The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.

- Release-bump carve-out (owner-authored `chore/release-v*`) unchanged and independent of the list.

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

Now: `isMachineAuthored(ticket, machineAuthor, owner)` which (a) is case-sensitive, (b) includes the release-bump carve-out (owner-authored `chore/release-v*` PRs now count as machine).

Effect of (b): for an owner-authored release-bump PR with validation-red, the SM would now try github_get_pr + parse body for `closes #N` + branch fallback — branch is `chore/release-vX.Y.Z`, which doesn't match `/gh-(\d+)$/` → linked stays null. Then below, presumably machine PRs with no linked issue... let me read further to see what happens when isMachinePr and linked==null. For a release-bump PR this now routes through the machine path. What does the machine path do differently vs guest path? Per the superseded 2026-10-04 comment: validation-red arms rework for guests too, PR-anchored. So the difference: machine PRs arm rework on the linked issue; guests get PR-anchored arm. For release-bump, linked is null → probably falls to the same PR-anchored arm. So effect may be minor but it's a semantic change not mentioned in the PR description ("Release-bump carve-out unchanged and independent of the list") — actually the carve-out in isMachineAuthored was pre-existing for the review guards; extending it to the rework re-arm is new behavior. Is it harmful? If a release-bump PR fails validation, now the machine tries to parse body for closing keywords — a release-bump body might contain "closes #..." rarely. Minor risk: it could arm rework on some issue referenced in the release notes. Edge case.

Also effect of (a) case-sensitivity: previously case-insensitive compare of ticket.author. If ticket.author arrives with different casing than config... GitHub API returns canonical login. Low risk.

2. postPRReviewComments.js: previously `prAuthor === machineAuthor` — strict, case-sensitive single compare, no carve-out. Now isMachineAuthored adds release-bump carve-out. Same semantic expansion. Consider: release-bump PRs are owner-authored; if review requests changes on them, previously: external path (verdict comment only). Now: re-arm agent:rework on the linked issue. A release bump rarely has a linked issue with "closes #N". So impact small. I'd classify SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT? The review verdict rules say IMPORTANT = real maintainability debt. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## PR Description

### What changed
The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.

### Key decisions
- `resolveMachineAuthor` still returns the raw config string; new `machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties, null → `[]` fail-closed); `isMachineAuthored` matches PR authors with a **case-sensitive** exact compare per entry; new `isMachineLogin()` gives the park probes their historical case-insensitive actor match across all entries.

- Release-bump carve-out (owner-authored `chore/release-v*`) unchanged and independent of the list.

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **PR #**: 730

- **Title**: gh-728 machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-728` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +353
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T06:40:33Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T06:40:58Z

## PR Description

### What changed
The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.

### Key decisions
- `resolveMachineAuthor` still returns the raw config string; new `machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties, null → `[]` fail-closed); `isMachineAuthored` matches PR authors with a **case-sensitive** exact compare per entry; new `isMachineLogin()` gives the park probes their historical case-insensitive actor match across all entries.
- Swept every direct single-login compare: the `fail_validation` rework re-arm in `smAgent.js`, both sticky-park RESET freshness checks, `parkResetCommit`'s machine-merge walk, the PR-anchored rework re-arm in `postPRReviewComments.js`, and `factoryState.js` `in_dev` assignment bucketing — all now route through the shared helpers.
- `.github/workflows/machine-sm.yml` input becomes `'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'`; module + factory docs updated.
- Release-bump carve-out (owner-authored `chore/release-v*`) unchanged and independent of the list.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
```
1566 pass; 3 failures in `release workflow wiring` are pre-existing on main (they assert on `agent-pack-release.yml`, untouched here).

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'"] --> RAW["resolveMachineAuthor (raw string)"]
  RAW --> LIST["machineAuthorLogins() -> [ai-teammate, github-actions[bot]]"]
  LIST --> AUTH["isMachineAuthored (PR authors, case-sensitive)"]
  LIST --> LOGIN["isMachineLogin (commit actors, case-insensitive)"]
  AUTH --> GUARDS["prMachineAuthor gate · notMachine filter · rework re-arms"]
  LOGIN --> PARK["sticky-park RESET / parkResetCommit walk"]
  LIST --> BUCKET["factoryState in_dev bucketing"]
```

</details>

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

Minor risk: it could arm rework on some issue referenced in the release notes. Edge case.

Also effect of (a) case-sensitivity: previously case-insensitive compare of ticket.author. If ticket.author arrives with different casing than config... GitHub API returns canonical login. Low risk.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? # gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

**Summary**: The gh-728 multi-login `machineAuthor` change is clean and well-tested — `machineAuthorLogins`/`isMachineLogin` fail closed, every direct single-login compare was swept (verified by grep: no remaining `=== machineAuthor` compares), docs and the workflow input were updated, and all changed-module unit tests pass (81/81 on `test_machineAuthor` + `test_factoryState`; failure set on the full suite is byte-identical to `origin/main`, so no regressions).

**Key Issues**: Two suggestion-level notes — the rework re-arm conversions (smAgent fail_validation, postPRReviewComments) pick up `isMachineAuthored`'s case-sensitive match and the release-bump carve-out, a subtle widening vs the old direct compares; and the factory-sm reusable workflow (external repo) should be confirmed to pass the comma list through untouched.

**Next Steps**:
1. Optional: pin the release-bump/case-sensitivity intent at the two converted call sites with a doc line or test.
2. Verify `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows` factory-sm.yml forwards `machine-author` verbatim (no single-login compare downstream).

💡 **SUGGESTION: Behavior change at this converted call site — carve-out + case sensitivity**

This replaced a case-insensitive single-login compare (`String(ticket.author).toLowerCase() === String(machineAuthor).toLowerCase()`) with `isMachineAuthored`, which changes two things beyond the intended list support:

1. **Release-bump carve-out is now active here.** An owner-authored `chore/release-v*` PR with red validation is now treated as a *machine* PR: it skips the guest-rework cap, enters the empty-lap withholding/escalation path, and probes the PR body for `closes|fixes|resolves #N` to re-arm `agent:rework`. On main this guard matched logins only. The other three `isMachineAuthored` call sites in smAgent (park probe, deferRedHead, self-heal) already had the carve-out, so this is *consistent* — but it is a widening the PR description doesn't mention ("Release-bump carve-out … unchanged"), and a release-notes body that happens to contain `closes #<n>` would now arm rework on that issue.

2. **Matching is now case-sensitive.** If a deployment writes the knob with non-canonical casing (e.g. `AI-Teammate`), a machine PR silently stops matching here and re-parks as a guest — the exact gh-728 failure mode. `isMachineLogin` (the actor probes) lowercases both sides; the author predicate deliberately does not.

Neither breaks the PR (authors arrive canonicalized from the API; release-bump branches `chore/release-v*` don't match the `gh-<n>` fallback and rarely carry closing keywords), but a one-line doc note at both converted call sites — or a test pinning "release-bump PR on red validation takes the machine path" — would make the intent explicit.

💡 **SUGGESTION: Same semantic widening as the smAgent fail_validation re-arm**

The old guard here was a strict single-login compare (`prAuthor === machineAuthor` — no release-bump carve-out). Routing through `isMachineAuthored` means an owner-authored `chore/release-v*` PR that receives REQUEST_CHANGES now gets `agent:rework` re-armed on its linked issue, where previously it took the external (report-only) path.

This is almost certainly the desired end state (the release flow is automated; the carve-out exists precisely so owner-authored release PRs ride the machine lane, and the sibling SM guards already include it), but it is a behavior change worth one assertion in `test_postPRReviewComments.js` — e.g. "release-bump PR + REQUEST_CHANGES → re-arm fires" — so a future refactor of `isMachineAuthored` can't quietly drop it.

### What changed
The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. 2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## PR Description

### What changed
The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.

- Release-bump carve-out (owner-authored `chore/release-v*`) unchanged and independent of the list.

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

Now: `isMachineAuthored(ticket, machineAuthor, owner)` which (a) is case-sensitive, (b) includes the release-bump carve-out (owner-authored `chore/release-v*` PRs now count as machine).

Effect of (b): for an owner-authored release-bump PR with validation-red, the SM would now try github_get_pr + parse body for `closes #N` + branch fallback — branch is `chore/release-vX.Y.Z`, which doesn't match `/gh-(\d+)$/` → linked stays null. Then below, presumably machine PRs with no linked issue... let me read further to see what happens when isMachinePr and linked==null. For a release-bump PR this now routes through the machine path. What does the machine path do differently vs guest path? Per the superseded 2026-10-04 comment: validation-red arms rework for guests too, PR-anchored. So the difference: machine PRs arm rework on the linked issue; guests get PR-anchored arm. For release-bump, linked is null → probably falls to the same PR-anchored arm. So effect may be minor but it's a semantic change not mentioned in the PR description ("Release-bump carve-out unchanged and independent of the list") — actually the carve-out in isMachineAuthored was pre-existing for the review guards; extending it to the rework re-arm is new behavior. Is it harmful? If a release-bump PR fails validation, now the machine tries to parse body for closing keywords — a release-bump body might contain "closes #..." rarely. Minor risk: it could arm rework on some issue referenced in the release notes. Edge case.

Also effect of (a) case-sensitivity: previously case-insensitive compare of ticket.author. If ticket.author arrives with different casing than config... GitHub API returns canonical login. Low risk.

2. postPRReviewComments.js: previously `prAuthor === machineAuthor` — strict, case-sensitive single compare, no carve-out. Now isMachineAuthored adds release-bump carve-out. Same semantic expansion. Consider: release-bump PRs are owner-authored; if review requests changes on them, previously: external path (verdict comment only). Now: re-arm agent:rework on the linked issue. A release bump rarely has a linked issue with "closes #N". So impact small. I'd classify SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT? The review verdict rules say IMPORTANT = real maintainability debt. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. - **Title**: gh-728 machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +353
- **Deletions**: -43
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T06:40:33Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T06:40:58Z

## PR Description

### What changed
The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.

### Key decisions
- `resolveMachineAuthor` still returns the raw config string; new `machineAuthorLogins()` splits it (trim + drop empties, null → `[]` fail-closed); `isMachineAuthored` matches PR authors with a **case-sensitive** exact compare per entry; new `isMachineLogin()` gives the park probes their historical case-insensitive actor match across all entries.
- Swept every direct single-login compare: the `fail_validation` rework re-arm in `smAgent.js`, both sticky-park RESET freshness checks, `parkResetCommit`'s machine-merge walk, the PR-anchored rework re-arm in `postPRReviewComments.js`, and `factoryState.js` `in_dev` assignment bucketing — all now route through the shared helpers.
- `.github/workflows/machine-sm.yml` input becomes `'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'`; module + factory docs updated.
- Release-bump carve-out (owner-authored `chore/release-v*`) unchanged and independent of the list.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
```
1566 pass; 3 failures in `release workflow wiring` are pre-existing on main (they assert on `agent-pack-release.yml`, untouched here).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'"] --> RAW["resolveMachineAuthor (raw string)"]
  RAW --> LIST["machineAuthorLogins() -> [ai-teammate, github-actions[bot]]"]
  LIST --> AUTH["isMachineAuthored (PR authors, case-sensitive)"]
  LIST --> LOGIN["isMachineLogin (commit actors, case-insensitive)"]
  AUTH --> GUARDS["prMachineAuthor gate · notMachine filter · rework re-arms"]
  LOGIN --> PARK["sticky-park RESET / parkResetCommit walk"]
  LIST --> BUCKET["factoryState in_dev bucketing"]
```

</details>

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

## Machine jobs

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

**Summary**: The gh-728 multi-login `machineAuthor` change is clean and well-tested — `machineAuthorLogins`/`isMachineLogin` fail closed, every direct single-login compare was swept (verified by grep: no remaining `=== machineAuthor` compares), docs and the workflow input were updated, and all changed-module unit tests pass (81/81 on `test_machineAuthor` + `test_factoryState`; failure set on the full suite is byte-identical to `origin/main`, so no regressions).

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: Behavior change at this converted call site — carve-out + case sensitivity**

This replaced a case-insensitive single-login compare (`String(ticket.author).toLowerCase() === String(machineAuthor).toLowerCase()`) with `isMachineAuthored`, which changes two things beyond the intended list support:

1. **Release-bump carve-out is now active here.** An owner-authored `chore/release-v*` PR with red validation is now treated as a *machine* PR: it skips the guest-rework cap, enters the empty-lap withholding/escalation path, and probes the PR body for `closes|fixes|resolves #N` to re-arm `agent:rework`. On main this guard matched logins only. The other three `isMachineAuthored` call sites in smAgent (park probe, deferRedHead, self-heal) already had the carve-out, so this is *consistent* — but it is a widening the PR description doesn't mention ("Release-bump carve-out … unchanged"), and a release-notes body that happens to contain `closes #<n>` would now arm rework on that issue.

2. **Matching is now case-sensitive.** If a deployment writes the knob with non-canonical casing (e.g. `AI-Teammate`), a machine PR silently stops matching here and re-parks as a guest — the exact gh-728 failure mode. `isMachineLogin` (the actor probes) lowercases both sides; the author predicate deliberately does not.

Neither breaks the PR (authors arrive canonicalized from the API; release-bump branches `chore/release-v*` don't match the `gh-<n>` fallback and rarely carry closing keywords), but a one-line doc note at both converted call sites — or a test pinning "release-bump PR on red validation takes the machine path" — would make the intent explicit.
","path":"/home/runner/work/dmtools-agents/dmtools-agents/outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: Same semantic widening as the smAgent fail_validation re-arm**

The old guard here was a strict single-login compare (`prAuthor === machineAuthor` — no release-bump carve-out). Routing through `isMachineAuthored` means an owner-authored `chore/release-v*` PR that receives REQUEST_CHANGES now gets `agent:rework` re-armed on its linked issue, where previously it took the external (report-only) path.

This is almost certainly the desired end state (the release flow is automated; the carve-out exists precisely so owner-authored release PRs ride the machine lane, and the sibling SM guards already include it), but it is a behavior change worth one assertion in `test_postPRReviewComments.js` — e.g. "release-bump PR + REQUEST_CHANGES → re-arm fires" — so a future refactor of `isMachineAuthored` can't quietly drop it.

### What changed
The `machineAuthor` deployment knob is now a comma-separated **list** of machine logins (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) instead of a single login, so CI-bot PRs (live fa PR #1249) ride the machine path: the conveyor reworks them on red instead of parking them as guests forever.

# gh-728: machineAuthor: support multiple machine logins (github-actions[bot] PRs park as guests forever)

## Description

**Live case: fa PR #1249** (ci(quarantine), authored by github-actions[bot]) — approved + reviewed, but parked with sticky validation_failed. The park resets ONLY on a human push (owner rule 2026-09-27), and the machine-author predicate (js/common/machineAuthor.js isMachineAuthored) matches a SINGLE login from jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (machine-sm.yml input: 'ai-teammate'). github-actions[bot] ≠ ai-teammate → the PR is a 'guest' → the conveyor can never unpark or rework it — it waits for a human push forever.

**Owner directive (2026-10-05):** github-actions-authored PRs must ride the machine path — the conveyor reworks them when they fail, same as ai-teammate PRs.

**Design:**
1. machineAuthor.js: resolveMachineAuthor keeps returning the raw config string, but isMachineAuthored treats it as a comma-separated LIST ('ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]') — trim + case-sensitive exact match per entry. Update the module docs (single-login assumption is baked into several comments).
2. machine-sm.yml (and any factory-sm consumer docs): machine-author input becomes 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'.
3. Tests: list parsing (single entry, multi entry, whitespace, no match), plus the #1249 scenario: github-actions[bot]-authored PR with red head → NOT parked (no validation_failed), re-enters on new head instead.
4. Sweep other author-keyed guards that hardcode one login (prMachineAuthor rules, notMachine filters) — they all ride isMachineAuthored, verify none compare against jobParams.machineAuthor directly.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

content.text:
Review complete. All outputs written to `outputs/`.

## Verdict: APPROVE (0 blocking · 0 important · 2 suggestions)

### What I reviewed
PR #730 (gh-728): `machineAuthor` deployment knob becomes a comma-separated **list** (`ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]`) so CI-bot PRs ride the machine path instead of parking as guests forever.

### Verification performed
- Read the full diff via `git diff origin/main...HEAD` (the provided `pr_diff.txt` was truncated mid-file).
- **Sweep check**: grepped for remaining direct single-login compares against `machineAuthor` — none left; all guards route through `machineAuthorLogins` / `isMachineLogin` / `isMachineAuthored`. Fail-closed on null/empty is preserved everywhere (park probes, bucketing, re-arms).
- **Test run** (node harness): `test_machineAuthor` + `test_factoryState` pass 81/81; the full-suite failure set is **byte-identical to `origin/main`** (48 pre-existing harness/env failures, incl. the known release-workflow ones) — zero PR-introduced failures, +22 new passing tests.
- Convention check (AGENTS.md): GraalJS style (`var`, no arrow functions) followed; YAML list value properly quoted.
- Ticket ACs: all four design points implemented, including the #1249 scenario tests (bot PR with red head → not parked; new head → re-enters validation).

### Findings (both SUGGESTION)
1. **`js/smAgent.js:2338`** — the converted `fail_validation` re-arm now inherits `isMachineAuthored`'s release-bump carve-out and case-sensitive match, vs the old case-insensitive login-only compare. Consistent with the three other smAgent call sites already on `isMachineAuthored`, but the widening is undocumented; non-canonical config casing would silently re-create the guest-park bug.
2. **`js/postPRReviewComments.js:1019`** — same widening: owner-authored release-bump PRs now get `agent:rework` re-armed on REQUEST_CHANGES. Almost certainly intended, but worth one pinning test.

Plus one general-comment note: the external `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows` factory-sm.yml should be confirmed to forward `machine-author` verbatim (no single-login compare downstream).
